papers.title: Dislocation Dynamics and Shape in High Entropy Alloys: the Influence of Stress Correlations, Long-Range Interactions and Anisotropy
papers.abstract: High entropy alloys gained significant scientific interest in recent years due to their enhanced mechanical properties including high yield strength combined with outstanding ductility. The strength of these materials originates from their highly heterogeneous pinning stress fields that hinder dislocation glide, that is, plastic deformation. This work investigates how the correlations and the anisotropy of the pinning stresses, and the long-range nature and the anisotropy of dislocation interactions influence the propagation of dislocations and the depinning transition in these alloys. Furthermore, it is studied how the impact of these factors manifest in the shape of dislocations. The implications to the wider scope of generic disordered systems and to possible experimental applications are also discussed.

summary_zh.motivation: 理解高熵合金中位错滑移的钉扎机制和形貌。
summary_zh.method: 采用理论模型分析应力场各向异性和长程相互作用的影响。
summary_zh.result: 揭示了应关联性和各向异性对位错传播和脱钉转变的影响。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，纯理论分析。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how stress correlations, long-range interactions, and anisotropy influence dislocation glide and depinning in high entropy alloys.
summary_en.method: Theoretical modeling of dislocation dynamics incorporating heterogeneous pinning stress fields and anisotropic dislocation interactions.
summary_en.result: Correlations and anisotropy of pinning stresses significantly affect dislocation shape and depinning transition.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely theoretical study.
